subject: Triton SIG: evidence for data retention and selective log-keep request
messages:
From: Emma Brooks <emma.brooks@tritonfin.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>; procurement@tritonfin.com
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG/CAIQ follow-up + retention ask

Hi Ava,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security team kicked off the SIG intake and attached a worksheet with a few follow-ups (see attached Triton_SIG_Questions.xlsx). Two items are urgent for our audit:

- Evidence that application-level request/response logs (including request metadata and request IDs) are retained for at least 12 months for customers on an enterprise plan, or a documented exception path.
- A sample export demonstrating we can obtain a time-ordered extract for a single tenant for forensic purposes.

We understand Redwood defaults to a 90-day rolling log retention for hosted environments; Triton requires 12 months for transaction-level logs for regulatory reasons. Can you confirm if Redwood supports a customer-specific retention exception, and if so what the operational and commercial processes look like (policy, evidence, timeline)?

I've cc'd procurement to flag there may be an amendment to our contract. SIG team would appreciate any evidence pack (retention policies, configuration snapshots, sample export) we can attach to the audit by May 24.

Thanks,
Emma Brooks
Senior Security Analyst | Triton Financial
emma.brooks@tritonfin.com
Attachments: Triton_SIG_Questions.xlsx (spreadsheet, 34KB)
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Emma Brooks <emma.brooks@tritonfin.com>
Cc: procurement@tritonfin.com
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG/CAIQ follow-up + retention ask

Emma —

Appreciate the detail and the worksheet. Short answer: we can support a customer-specific retention amendment for transactional logs (hosted) under Dedicated/Enterprise commitments; for hosted customers we typically evaluate on a case-by-case basis because of storage and isolation implications.

What I will do:
- Loop in our security evidence owner for the specific artifacts you requested.
- Share a sample export and our retention policy extract.
- Draft a one-off retention amendment (operational SLA + expected cost) for Triton to review.

Can you confirm whether Triton needs the export to include PII redaction or if a full exercise tenant export is fine for the audit? That affects the sample. If you can confirm by EOD Wed (May 19) we'll target to get the evidence pack to you by May 24.

I'll be in touch with a follow-up and the evidence pack link.

Best,
Ava Chen

Quoted below is the original email from their security contact.

Can you advise:
- Marissa: what artifacts we can provide as evidence this week? Specifically: retention policy extract (config), a sample time-ordered export for a single tenant (with redaction guidance), and any operational runbook entries that describe how we execute a retention exception. Also note whether the sample requires Dedicated or if we can produce an exported archive from hosted for auditing purposes.
- Rishi: if we need to offer a retention amendment, what are the commercial levers (storage surcharge, SLA note, lead time)? Please provide a ballpark so I can include it in the draft amendment.

Attachments I'm planning to send to Triton: retention-evidence-2027.pdf (evidence pack stub), redwood-retention-amendment-draft.docx (amendment with sample language). I'll export a sample log csv if Marissa confirms it's safe to include in the pack.

Thanks — want to get this out to Triton with proposed language by Thu EOD so they can include it in their audit packet.

— Ava

Subject: Triton: retention evidence pack + proposed amendment (doc + sample export)

Hi Emma —

Thanks for the quick turnaround on scope. Per our discussion and internal verification, attached is a preliminary evidence pack and a draft one-off amendment to capture a 12-month transactional-log retention for Triton. Highlights:

- Evidence pack (retention-evidence-2027.pdf): policy extract, retention configuration snapshot (hosted default), and a redacted sample export of a tenant's request/response log (CSV). The sample export includes request_ids and timestamps; we redacted content payloads and customer PII.
- Draft amendment (redwood-retention-amendment-draft.docx): proposed contractual language, estimated monthly storage surcharge, and suggested acceptance criteria for export requests.
- Process: once Triton signs the amendment (DocuSign link below), our ops team will schedule a configuration change and provide the first 12-month export within 10 business days. Exports for forensic requests thereafter will be handled via a secure transfer.

DocuSign link to amendment: https://www.docusign.com/transactions/XYZ-TR-2027-87
Drive link to evidence pack: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cRedwoodEvidencePack

Attachments: retention-evidence-2027.pdf (pdf, 780KB), redwood-retention-amendment-draft.docx (docx, 28KB), sample-tenant-export.csv (csv, 145KB)

Next steps: Please confirm whether the redacted sample export meets Triton's audit needs and whether procurement wants us to add the amendment to the existing MSA or as an SOW addendum. If you sign the amendment via the DocuSign link we'll begin the configuration change.

If helpful, Marissa is available for a short call to walk through the artifacts and answer SIG-specific questions.
